# Aunt Jamesina

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v3 c16 P24](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0024), [v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052)</sub>
- **Role:** Housekeeper for college students  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Aunt Jimsie  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c19 P41](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0041)</sub>; Aunty  <sub>[v3 c19 P1](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0001), [v3 c25 P3](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0003)</sub>; Aunty J.  <sub>[v3 c24 P5](../source/v03-c24.md#nw-v03-c24-p0005)</sub>

## Appearance

She is a tiny old woman with snow-white hair worn in quaint little puffs over her ears, pink cheeks, and a softly-triangular face. She has large, soft blue eyes filled with youth and hope. She dresses in an old-fashioned style.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)_

## Personality

Aunt Jamesina is sweet, cheerful, and old-fashioned in her habits and opinions, though she remains youthful and bright in spirit. She possesses a lively sense of humor and tolerantly allows the young women in her care to act freely without imposing rigid discipline. She holds traditional views, especially regarding ministers and proper conduct, yet she enjoys a good laugh and speaks her mind candidly and kindly.

_Sources: [v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c16 P64](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0064), [v3 c19 P4](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0004), [v3 c25 P13](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0013), [v3 c35 P5](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0005), [v3 c35 P21](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0021)_

- Old-fashioned  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)</sub>
- Cheerful and youthful in spirit  <sub>[v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052), [v3 c19 P4](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0004)</sub>

## Abilities

- Knitting  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c25 P2](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0002)</sub>
- Housekeeping and mothering  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c37 P12](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0012)</sub>

## Goals

- To keep house for the girls at Patty's Place in Kingsport  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>
- To get a yellow silk dress in heaven  <sub>[v3 c19 P6](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0006)</sub>

## History

Aunt Jamesina was named after her father, who drowned shortly before her birth. After her daughter married and departed for foreign mission work, she found herself lonely in her large home. When Philippa Gordon proposed renting a house in Kingsport for college, Aunt Jamesina moved in to serve as housekeeper for Philippa, Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, and Stella Maynard at Patty's Place. She brought along her two cats, the Sarah-cat and Joseph, and later helped care for the stray cat Rusty. She remained at Patty's Place during holidays to tend to the cats and house plants. When the girls graduated from Redmond College, she decided to take all three cats home with her so they would not be separated.

_Sources: [v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c16 P55](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0055), [v3 c16 P58](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0058), [v3 c18 P0](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0000), [v3 c18 P1](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0001), [v3 c18 P24](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0024), [v3 c38 P8](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0008)_

## Background by volume

- Her father, James, was drowned at sea a month before she was born, leading to her name  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>
- She had a daughter, Elizabeth, who became a missionary  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c27 P6](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0006), [v3 c36 P11](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0011)</sub>
- Her husband passed away and she was left living alone in a large house  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c19 P6](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0006)</sub>
- Was given the Sarah-cat by her washerwoman eight years prior  <sub>[v3 c16 P58](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0058), [v3 c16 P59](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0059)</sub>

## Quotes

> New shoes are smarter than old ones, but the old ones are more comfortable. I’m old enough to indulge myself in the matter of shoes and opinions.  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)</sub>

> The very first thing I’m going to do when I get to heaven is to get a yellow silk dress.  <sub>[v3 c19 P6](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0006)</sub>

> Do your duty by God and your neighbor and yourself, and have a good time. That’s my philosophy and it’s always worked pretty well.  <sub>[v3 c19 P4](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0004)</sub>

> Kittens have to be drowned, I admit, or the world would be overrun. But no decent, grown-up cat should be done to death—unless he sucks eggs.  <sub>[v3 c16 P69](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0069)</sub>

> People who haven’t natural gumption never learn, neither in college nor life.  <sub>[v3 c37 P26](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0026)</sub>
